blockers.title: RPM materialization still begins from an undefined blob and does not preserve one file identity across hash, checksig, and extraction
evidence: selectionKey produces only a unique NEVRA. materialization.write then says to write the unique rpmdb package blob for that NEVRA, but no rpmdb query, librpm API, repository object, archive pathname, descriptor, or byte-returning membership rule produces that blob. Moving the same undefined noun into a write step does not satisfy PTCB-V24-B1's required acquisition.

The destination ceremony explicitly fsyncs and closes the newly created file. O_EXCL proves only that the destination did not exist at creation; the candidate gives run-owned directory no owner/mode/descriptor grammar and retains no device, inode, link count, directory descriptor, or held file descriptor after close.

identity re-hashes the pathname immediately before rpm --checksig and immediately before rpm2cpio, but neither command is followed by a hash/identity check and no descriptor is passed into them. A pathname replacement between the pre-command hash and the command's open is therefore unobserved. The prose MUST NOT be replaced is a desired property, not an operation that detects or prevents replacement.

A concrete race satisfies every recorded check: materialize expected archive A and hash A; after the pre-checksig hash, substitute a different validly signed RPM B for rpm --checksig; restore A for the pre-rpm2cpio hash; substitute B again for rpm2cpio. Both observed hashes equal A's signed digest, checksig succeeds on B, and authenticatedManifest is derived from B. No post-open hash or inode record detects the swaps.

The branch also never compares the internal NEVRA of the materialized archive with selectionKey/authenticityCore.name+version. rpm --checksig authenticates whichever signed RPM occupies the pathname; signature success alone does not supply the omitted package-identity equality.
blockers.impact: The v25 destination path fixes raw bytes in argv but not the source or same-file chain. RPM-family profiles can still have no lawful archive source, or can retain packagePayloadDigest for A while verifying/extracting B, allowing an authenticated manifest unrelated to the signed package identity to drive later object admission.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define one real archive acquisition with an exact byte-returning API or immutable source object and bind its internal NEVRA to selectionKey and authenticityCore. Keep the archive on one held descriptor, or define a protected directory plus openat/O_NOFOLLOW device+inode identity and post-command revalidation that proves rpm/librpm and rpm2cpio consumed the hashed file. Prefer a descriptor-capable librpm verification/extraction API; if pathname materialization is unavoidable, specify ownership/mode, safe filename encoding, before-and-after inode/digest checks, and retained evidence for every open.

blockers.title: Withdrawing Linux pathless authentication while retaining Linux in slice 1 makes every Linux profile unqualifiable
evidence: The IMA false allow is genuinely removed: linux-pathless is WITHDRAWN-THIS-GENERATION and every Linux PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED entry refuses. That is fail-closed, but it is not a complete Linux OS-ABI identity rule.
platforms.slice1 still contains linux/x86_64 and linux/arm64, and the two Linux platformProfile stems remain reserved for later population. No rostered change removes or defers either D-002 platform.

OS ABI remains a mandatory taxonomy member. pathlessClasses says OS ABI MUST use PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED and linuxStanding says that exact combination refuses this generation. No DIGEST-BOUND, INSTALL-ROOT, EXTERNAL, absent, or inapplicable alternative is lawful for the cell.

G22 requires every complete platformProfile times every taxonomy class, while NT-TCB-1 says inability to observe/substitute is a qualification failure or platform-removal path, not a skipped cell. v25 records the qualification failure but takes no platform-removal path.

The DR-126 row calls for closed OS-ABI identity rules and the artifact purpose is to lock the qualitative TCB shape. Deferring the only Linux OS-ABI rule to an unspecified successor leaves that qualitative shape absent for half of the named slice-1 OS/architecture stems.
blockers.impact: No Linux slice-1 profile can ever complete its mandatory OS-ABI cell or the G22 matrix under v25, regardless of how later selector and allowlist tables are populated. The candidate is safe against the v24 IMA attack only by making the declared Linux platform contract impossible to qualify.
blockers.requiredRepair: Specify the measured-boot executing-kernel ceremony needed for Linux pathless authentication, or obtain an authorized product/platform decision that removes or defers Linux and consistently updates platforms.slice1, profile stems, G22 scope, and related mappings. A DR-126 candidate cannot silently retain Linux as slice-1 scope while withdrawing its mandatory OS-ABI identity rule.

shouldFix.title: The repaired path join says hash uniqueness is unnecessary while two live manifest rules still require it
evidence: joinMust now correctly says hash uniqueness of the whole manifest is not required once path+hash selects the member. matchedManifestMember still says duplicate relativePath or sha256 in the manifest refuses.

authenticatedManifest.uniqueness independently still says that if two members share a sha256 or a relativePath, refuse. There is no precedence or supersession rule for these contradictory live requirements.

A package with canonical paths a and b containing identical regular-file bytes has one unambiguous path+hash member for an opened a. joinMust admits it, while both surviving uniqueness rules refuse it.

honestyRepairsFromV24 claims whole-manifest hash uniqueness is not required, overstating the normative edit. The APT wiring, one-leading-./ strip, component rejection, and soleGrammar connections are real, but this required part of PTCB-V24-S1 was not applied.

The EXTERNAL transform also remains open: signed canonicalOrigin is defined as a full object path, while packageRelativePathRule asks whether the object is under it and then strips that directory prefix. No dirname derivation or directory-prefix field defines the referenced prefix.
shouldFix.impact: Validators can disagree on ordinary packages with duplicate contents, and EXTERNAL package members can receive different relativePath bytes. The same archive/event can therefore qualify or refuse depending on which live sentence and path derivation an implementation chooses.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Delete sha256 uniqueness from matchedManifestMember and authenticatedManifest; require only unique canonical relativePath/member entries, since joinMust compares both path and hash. Add an explicit supersession statement. For EXTERNAL, define the exact directory derivation from the full canonicalOrigin or replace it with a signed archive-root-relative mapping, including root and boundary behavior.

shouldFix.title: rpmHeaderIdentity is neither gated to RPM events nor explicitly equal to the retained query output
evidence: rpmHeaderIdentity is an optional member of the generic linux-file-backed tag, whose when-clause covers every Linux package-db event. No rule permits it only when observedPlatformAttestation.trustDecision.interfaceId is rpm-checksig or forbids it for apt-secure.

headerIdentity.retainedField names rpmHeaderIdentity when present, but no normative equality says rpmHeaderIdentity.sha256header MUST equal the exact 64-hex output of headerIdentity.queryArgv for this event's NEVRA.

Consequently an apt-secure Debian/Ubuntu event may carry an arbitrary syntactically valid rpmHeaderIdentity, and an RPM event may carry a value different from the query output, without violating the closed tag or the use prohibition.
The field is correctly prohibited from affecting packagePayloadDigest/authenticityCore, so this is not a false allow. It is still an open provenance branch inside the retained qualification evidence.
shouldFix.impact: The same closed event shape admits meaningless cross-interface metadata and cannot reproduce whether a retained RPM header identity came from the named query. Independent trace validators can accept incompatible evidence records.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Gate rpmHeaderIdentity on trustDecision.interfaceId=rpm-checksig and forbid it for apt-secure. When present, require byte equality to the normalized output of headerIdentity.queryArgv for the same selected NEVRA and bind that NEVRA/query to the containing event association token.

verdictBasis: REJECT: 2 blockers and 2 SHOULD-FIX findings. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
conclusion: REJECT. v25 removes the IMA false allow, uses real pathname operands for RPM tools, wires APT and the opened-object join to one member-path grammar, and cleans up SHA256HEADER's role. It still assumes an undefined RPM source and releases file identity across path-based commands; it also retains Linux as slice-1 scope while making its mandatory OS-ABI cell impossible. Conflicting manifest hash-uniqueness rules and an ungated, unbound rpmHeaderIdentity keep the retained evidence open. DR-126 remains OPEN; no DR is marked SATISFIED, and no D-096 (A) grant, G22 qualification, sealing, application, or implementation authority is created.
